html:
SMTO-EXE-0028 — SMTO couldn't find a value where it was told to look

GUID: 683f7e3b-0b2e-4aee-9070-da771a455602
Slug: json-pointer-invalid
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO tried to pick out one value from a saved result or a sign-in reply, but the location it was given doesn't exist there. The step that needed that value didn't run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you were saving sign-in settings for a web service connection in your saved Parameters, make each Extraction path whose Source is json start with a slash, for example /token. SMTO only accepts these paths when they start at the top of the sign-in reply, which the leading slash means.
  2. Check that each name in that path matches the sign-in reply exactly, including capital letters. SMTO looks for the exact name, so a small spelling difference means nothing is found.
  3. If this happened during a task, ask SMTO in the conversation to look at the earlier step's result again and use a value that is actually there. The earlier result is saved, so SMTO can pick the right value without running that step again.

What success looks like

  • The connection saves without this message, or the task step that needed the value runs.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't type in a made-up value to get past this; the step would work with wrong information.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An RFC 6901 JSON Pointer was malformed (bad ~ escape, missing leading slash, non-canonical index) or selected a missing key, an out-of-range index or a path through a scalar; HTTP login JSON extraction paths must start with '/'.

What this means

  • Exact JSON-pointer resolution rejected malformed syntax or escaping, an absent object key, invalid/out-of-range array index or traversal through a scalar; HTTP JSON extraction also requires its supported rooted path form. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Exact JSON-pointer resolution rejected malformed syntax or escaping, an absent object key, invalid/out-of-range array index or traversal through a scalar; HTTP JSON extraction also requires its supported rooted path form.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact retained JSON shape and each decoded pointer token, including ~0 and ~1 escaping and array index rules.

How to fix it

  • For tool input_bindings, compare source_pointer against the stored receipt data for source_operation_id and use an existing key or index with ~0 and ~1 escaping (agent_runtime.execution.json_pointer.resolve_pointer). For HTTP connection profiles, make every login extract rule with source 'json' use a rooted pointer such as /token (gateway_core.http_auth.config.validate_auth). Never fabricate the value or rerun the producing step just to create the path.
  • Inspect the exact retained JSON structure and use an existing key/index with correct ~0 and ~1 escapes. Do not fabricate evidence or replay an operation to make a pointer valid.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The corrected pointer resolves the intended existing value without guessing, fabricating data or replaying its producer.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
